content: @Fabrizio Montesi Do you envision that all temporal logics in cslib will be extensions of cslib#927? I have a concern about this, because some of the most useful temporal logics for reasoning about programs do not need the past-time operators, which cslib#927 has. An example is Lamport's TLA.

No, I don't -- as you point out, things like TLA are not extensions of BTL. BTL in that PR is mostly a nice thing to have, plus a sanity check that it works as expected in the generic modal framework.

When we're happy with it (it follows strictly the textbook presentation, modulo the generalisation of DiagonalInverse for reusability in other logics), I was planning on polishing the encoding of LTL, which is separate (that's a new result not in the literature, so I wanna be a bit paranoid about its adequacy...).
Thanks for the explanation. I'll review your LTL PR when it's ready.

Sounds good!

It'd be helpful to get a review of cslib#927 for that first, at least in particular regarding notation of operators and judgements, since I'll follow a similar (albeit separate) line for LTL.
I ran out of time today. (Two big PRs to review.). I'll review cslib#927 tomorrow.
